summary: Frontend-only bug fix verified: not_responding POST now carries phone coords so a red map marker appears immediately (before user taps I'm Safe). E2E on Expo web (390x844) with page.route intercepting POST https://safequake.onrender.com/api/status AND ${EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL}/api/trigger-alert (both mocked 200). TEST 1 — permission GRANTED @ Mriehel, Malta (35.8916, 14.4658, accuracy=10): tapping trigger-alert-btn produced 3 status POSTs in order [not_responding, not_responding, safe] (within the allowed 1..3 total). The initial not_responding POST fired with location.error='no_cached_fix' (web has no last-known cache), then the background Location.getCurrentPositionAsync BestForNavigation branch resolved within ~30ms and re-POSTed not_responding with ALL fanned-out coord fields populated exactly to spec: latitude=35.8916, longitude=14.4658, lat=35.8916, lng=14.4658, lon=14.4658, coords={latitude:35.8916,longitude:14.4658,accuracy:10}, coordinates=[14.4658,35.8916], geo={type:'Point',coordinates:[14.4658,35.8916]}, location.latitude=35.8916, location.longitude=14.4658, location.error=null. Navigation to /alert happened immediately (alert-screen mounted while background refresh completed — router.push does NOT block). Tapping im-safe-btn on /alert triggered exactly 1 safe POST with warm GPS fix (35.8916,14.4658,±10m) — alert-success-toast appeared and app auto-navigated back to Home. Also observed: exactly 1 POST to /api/trigger-alert with {triggeredBy:'qg-...', magnitude:6.4, distance_km:12, intensity:'VII'}. TEST 2 — permission DENIED (page.context.clear_permissions()): tapping trigger-alert-btn produced 1 not_responding POST with location={latitude:null,longitude:null,accuracy:null,error:'permission_denied'} AND top-level latitude/lat/lng/lon/coords/coordinates/geo keys ALL ABSENT (checkin.ts only fans them out when lat!==null — verified), and navigation to /alert still proceeded (graceful degradation confirmed). CODE-LEVEL CHECKS on /app/frontend/app/index.tsx all PASS: import * as Location from 'expo-location' (L7); handleTrigger calls Location.hasServicesEnabledAsync (L77) → getForegroundPermissionsAsync (L79) → requestForegroundPermissionsAsync when canAskAgain (L83) → getLastKnownPositionAsync({maxAge:120_000, requiredAccuracy:500}) (L94-97); initial postStatus fires with lastKnown coords OR error-only location (never omitted) (L103-124); background refresh: if permGranted && (!lastKnown || accuracy>100) fires Location.getCurrentPositionAsync({accuracy:Location.Accuracy.BestForNavigation}) then re-POSTs not_responding with fresh coords (L129-159); broadcastAlert() unawaited (L163), ensureNotificationSetup + scheduleCheckInReminders (L167-173), router.push('/alert') + setTriggering(false) (L175-176). REGRESSION: sticky trigger-alert-btn swaps to ActivityIndicator during triggering (Pressable L267-284), 4 tip cards render (drop/cover/hold on/after — L221-240), alert screen im-safe-btn POSTs safe with warm GPS fix and cancelCheckInReminders() runs on success (alert.tsx L214-224).

critical_code_review_comments: index.tsx L129: background refresh gate uses (!lastKnown || accuracy>100). On web, getLastKnownPositionAsync returned null so the background branch fires — good. On native with a fresh cached fix within 500m accuracy, only the first POST fires (no duplicate) — also good.

index.tsx L124: initial postStatus is fire-and-forget with .catch(() => {}) so a network failure won't block navigation. Background refresh (L135) uses `await postStatus(...)` inside an IIFE which is also fire-and-forget from the outer scope — behaviour intended.

checkin.ts L60: top-level lat/lng/lon/coords/coordinates/geo are only added when BOTH lat AND lng are non-null. Verified in TEST 2 that permission_denied path yields payloads WITHOUT these keys — matches spec exactly. `location.latitude/longitude` remain null in the nested location object so downstream schemas can still read the error state.

handleTrigger sets setTriggering(false) synchronously AFTER router.push (L175-176). This is fine because the Home screen unmounts on navigation; but on error paths it prevents the button from being stuck disabled if the user backs out via router.back(). No issue.

Expo web preview logs '[expo-notifications] Listening to push token changes not yet fully supported on web' and 'shadow* deprecated, use boxShadow'. Both are expected on web and do not affect native builds. No deprecated packages (expo-av, expo-barcode-scanner, expo-background-fetch) detected.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Bug fix for immediate map-marker on trigger is fully verified on Expo web. On web, Location.getLastKnownPositionAsync returns null (no cache) so the initial not_responding POST carries error='no_cached_fix' — this is EXPECTED and the spec explicitly accepts it, provided the background BestForNavigation refresh follows with populated coords within 5s (verified). Total status POSTs range: 2 (permission_denied) or 3 (granted, no cache). On native devices with a warm cache, expect 1 not_responding POST (with coords) + 1 safe POST = 2 total.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: dashboard map showed the not_responding count but no red marker because the initial POST from Home carried no coords. Root cause: handleTrigger only ran GPS on the /alert screen (im-safe path), not at trigger time. Fix in index.tsx: on trigger, immediately call getLastKnownPositionAsync (instant, 120s cache, 500m accuracy) and post not_responding WITH coords; if cache missing or too coarse, kick off a background getCurrentPositionAsync(BestForNavigation) and re-post not_responding with the fresh fix. checkin.ts fans lat/lng into every schema shape (latitude, lat, lng, lon, coords, coordinates, geo.coordinates) so any dashboard schema will pick up the marker. Verified end-to-end above.
